I will keep the same wheat-maize rotation on all 1.5 mu, because that is what fits my land, my well water, and my labor. I do not farm enough area to gamble with fancy changes. I will start from what has worked in recent years in south Hebei: stable wheat, then stable summer maize, and I will push fertilizer a little on the safe side because losing yield hurts more than spending a bit extra on inputs. Since I have high education and I have farmed 15 years, I do not just copy blindly, but I still look at what works locally. On this kind of small irrigated land, I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed, keep phosphorus steady for root growth, keep enough nitrogen for yield, and give potassium mainly to hold the crop up and fill grain better. Wheat needs tighter management because overwintering and spring regrowth decide the final harvest, so I will irrigate it three times if the season is normal. Summer maize grows in the rainy season, but rain is never something I fully trust, so with well irrigation I will plan for two irrigations and adjust if rain is enough. On pesticide, I will not spray casually, but I will not wait too long either; on 1.5 mu, one bad disease or insect flush is enough to cost real grain. For tillage, I will keep it simple and efficient: rotary tillage before wheat after maize residue handling, and no-tillage or very light direct seeding for summer maize if conditions allow, because that saves time between the two crops.
